title: LYON
43 BC TO NOW

cards.title: A colony on the hill
lines: Lucius Munatius Plancus, a former officer of Julius Caesar, is credited with founding the Roman colony of Lugdunum.
The date of 43 BC is traditional; scholars still debate it.

cards.title: Water for the hill
lines: The Monts d'Or aqueduct, completed around 20 BC, is the first of at least four that serve the city.

cards.title: An emperor is born
lines: Claudius is born in Lugdunum in 10 BC and returns often, especially during the conquest of Britain (AD 43–47).

cards.title: The martyrs
lines: In AD 177 Christians die in the amphitheatre on the Croix-Rousse slope, among them Pothinus, the first bishop of Lyon.
Sources count about 40 to 48 victims.
cards.target: Roman Condate and Three Gauls slope

cards.title: Saint-Jean rises
lines: Work on the cathedral begins in 1180 on the ruins of a 6th-century church.
It will take almost three centuries.

cards.title: A council in Lyon
lines: Saint-Jean hosts the First Council of Lyon; a second council follows in 1274.
cards.note: S11 nomina i due concili ma la pagina letta non ne riporta l'anno: date da verificare

cards.title: Fairs and bankers
lines: Under Louis XI (1461–83) four annual fairs are founded.
Florentine immigrants turn Lyon into a financial centre.

cards.title: Silk comes to Lyon
lines: Francis I grants weaving privileges that had been an Italian monopoly.
Silk will shape the city for the next three centuries.
cards.note: S2 non riporta l'anno: 1536 da verificare

cards.title: A pasture becomes a square
lines: Henry IV orders the city to buy a former pasture for a new public space.
A long lawsuit follows.

cards.title: The king in bronze
lines: The first statue of Louis XIV is made in 1713.
By 1715 the square is the Place Royale.

cards.title: Lyon against Paris
lines: Lyon sides with the Girondists against the National Convention.
From 9 August 1793 the Army of the Alps besieges the city.

cards.title: The city surrenders
lines: On 9 October the civil authorities surrender at midday.
The royalist leader Précy has escaped at dawn through Vaise.

cards.title: Ville-Affranchie
lines: On 12 October the Convention decrees the demolition of the homes of the rich and renames the city.
Of 600 houses planned for demolition, only about fifty fall.

cards.title: Bellecour loses its king
lines: The bronze statue of Louis XIV, raised in 1713, is destroyed in 1793.

cards.title: A mechanism for the loom
lines: A prize for loom improvements leads to Jacquard's mechanism.
Lyon has 41 Jacquard looms in 1811 and 1,879 by 1820.

cards.title: A belt of forts
lines: Work begins in 1830 on a ring of fortifications around the city.
Later it will also help to watch Croix-Rousse.

cards.title: The canuts take the city
lines: Falling silk prices have cut the weavers' wages.
On 22 November 1831 they seize Lyon; on 3 December Marshal Soult retakes it with 20,000 men.
cards.note: S14 data la prima rivolta a ottobre 1831; S3 (22 nov-3 dic) e' piu' preciso

cards.title: The cost
lines: The fighting leaves about 100 soldiers and 69 civilians dead.
The minimum price the weavers wanted is abolished afterwards.

cards.title: The bloody week
lines: The second revolt starts on 9 April 1834. Barricades rise and the army bombards Croix-Rousse.
By 15 April the city is retaken.

cards.title: A fort to watch the hill
lines: Afterwards the government builds a fort to separate Croix-Rousse from the rest of Lyon.
cards.note: S3 non dà l'anno della costruzione

cards.title: The first power loom
lines: The first power loom is installed in 1843.
By 1866 Lyon counts 30,000 looms, with 95,000 more in the countryside.

cards.title: Three towns join Lyon
lines: Vaise, La Croix-Rousse and La Guillotière are annexed in 1852.
The city jumps to 234,531 people.

cards.title: The city crosses the Rhône
lines: Two big waves of building, in 1853 and 1862, push the city east onto the left bank.

cards.title: The Rhône breaks out
lines: In late May 1856 the river floods the new left-bank districts.
In La Guillotière alone 18 people die.
cards.note: la data della rottura dell'argine varia tra fonti (29-30 maggio o 31 maggio-1 giugno), non verificata su fonte primaria

cards.title: The emperor visits
lines: Napoleon III visits Lyon on 2 June 1856 and a decree grants the city 300,000 francs.
Édouard Baldus is sent to photograph the damage.

cards.title: Under Fourvière
lines: A railway tunnel under Fourvière links the Paris line to the station at Perrache (1857).

cards.title: A street through the Presqu'île
lines: Benoît Poncet completes the Rue Impériale in the 1850s, today's Rue de la République.
It cuts a straight line through the old streets.
cards.note: S8 dice solo 'anni 1850'; anno esatto non verificato

cards.title: A vow in stone
lines: After Lyon is spared in the war of 1870, the community commits to build a basilica on Fourvière.
Work starts in 1872, paid by private funds.

cards.title: The basilica stands
lines: The building is finished in 1884; decoration goes on until 1896.

cards.title: The bridges fall
lines: Between 1 and 3 September 1944 retreating German forces blow up bridges across the Saône and the Rhône.
The Pont d'Ainay is never rebuilt.

cards.title: Lyon is free
lines: On 3 September 1944 US and French forces liberate the city.

cards.title: Lafayette reopens
lines: The Pont Lafayette, its central arch destroyed in 1944, reopens in 1946.

cards.title: Pont Pasteur reopens
lines: Destroyed by German forces on 2 September 1944, the bridge reopens in 1952.

cards.title: Barracks into business
lines: In 1960 the State sells the Part-Dieu barracks land.
Demolition of the old buildings lasts five years.

cards.title: The metro
lines: Line C opens in 1974; lines A and B follow in 1978.

cards.title: Europe's biggest urban mall
lines: The Part-Dieu shopping centre and the Auditorium open in 1975.
At the time it is the largest urban mall in Europe.

cards.title: A world heritage hill
lines: Croix-Rousse is part of the area inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1998.
cards.note: S14 parla di 'area'; il sito UNESCO e' piu' ampio: da verificare

cards.title: Part-Dieu again
lines: In 2014 the Metropolis launches a renewal programme of about 2.5 billion euros.

cards.title: Where two rivers meet
lines: The Musée des Confluences opens on 20 December 2014 at the southern tip of the Presqu'île.

cards.title: Lyon today
lines: The commune of Lyon counts 519,127 people in the 2023 census.
